messages:
omar: Running the Docker quickstart in corp network and my container can't complete the 'first call' step. curl inside container returns 'Proxy Authentication Required' but the host app shows 401 from API.
kelly: Is the container inheriting the corporate HTTP_PROXY env? That can cause a 407 from the proxy upstream. What's the exact curl output?
omar: From inside container: 
```\n$ curl -v https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/health -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\"\n* Connected to proxy.company (10.0.0.5) port 8080 (#0)\n> CONNECT api.play.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1\n> Proxy-Authorization: Negotiate TlRMTVNTUAAB...\n< HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required\n< Proxy-Authenticate: NTLM\n```\nSo the proxy returns 407 but our quickstart code logs only 'request failed: unauthorized' later when the client library retries, which made me think my API key was bad.
mike: Right, transparent proxies that do auth can rewrite traffic and cause the TLS handshake to fail or return 407 pre-TLS. We should surface the proxy error earlier. Also curious why you see a 401 in the app logs?
omar: The server logs show a 401 event for session.create after several retries. I think the client retried without proxy auth and then backend returned billing blocked: {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"}. It was confusing because I didn't see the 407 in the initial quickstart output.
kelly: Two things to fix: 1) quickstart README needs a corp-proxy troubleshooting section (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY, NTLM caveats, docker run -e to pass env). 2) client lib should bubble up non-application-level HTTP codes from the transport layer (407, 502) and not swallow them as generic auth failures.
omar: Repro steps: 
- docker run --rm -e HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.company:8080 -e REDWOOD_KEY=$KEY redwood/quickstart 
- inside container: curl -v https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
observed 407 then later client shows 'unauthorized' + 'billing_required' combo.
lee: I'll add a short FAQ entry: "Why does first call fail behind corporate proxy?" with examples: passing proxy creds, using an outbound egress rule for dev machines, or running quickstart with --network host to avoid proxy in dev. Also add an explicit note that billing gating will return 402/403 depending on flow and can appear after retries.
mike: Filed DEVEX-1137 to track client logging changes: "preserve transport errors and surface proxy auth (407) vs backend 401/402". assigning to me.
devex-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1137 "client: surface proxy transport errors separately from auth/billing"  assigned to mike
omar: thx. Workaround for folks: run quickstart locally without proxy env or ensure the workspace has billing enabled. Also run curl with -x http://proxy.company:8080 -U user:pass to reproduce.
kelly: I pushed a tiny README PR with troubleshooting snippets and a note about corporate proxies and billing gates. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart/pull/62
mike: will follow up and add a small HA test to make sure retries don't mask transport-level errors. Closing once PR merges.
